issues.label: Headline overstates culture-negative as "not an infection"
issues.as_written: Half of urinary tract infections diagnosed in the ER weren't infections at all
issues.abstract_says: Of 658 ED-diagnosed UTIs, only 354 (54%) had significant bacterial growth in urine cultures. ... In ED UTIs are frequently overdiagnosed in older adults
issues.problem: 46% lacked significant bacterial growth, which the authors call overdiagnosis rather than proof of no infection; "weren't infections at all" is a stronger claim than a negative culture supports, and 46% is slightly under "half."
issues.suggested_fix: Reword to "Nearly half of ER-diagnosed urinary tract infections had no significant bacterial growth" or "were likely overdiagnosed."

fact_check.headline: A simple five-part checkup of body and mind predicted dementia across 49,000 people in three countries
fact_check.notes: Cohort names and sizes, the five intrinsic capacity domains, the graded hazard ratios (1.31/1.65/2.41 reported as 31%/65%/141% higher), the C-index improvement and psychological functioning as the most consistent domain all match the abstract.

fact_check.headline: Education and mentally demanding work predicted better everyday functioning — in people whose thinking tested completely normal
fact_check.notes: N, mean age, sex split, 42% global and 49% applied-cognitive impairment reductions, and education's mediation to quality of life are all correct; the headline credits occupational complexity more than the abstract does, and two caveat details aren't in the abstract.

issues.label: Headline attributes effect to occupational complexity
issues.as_written: Education and mentally demanding work predicted better everyday functioning
issues.abstract_says: Among CR domains, education showed the most consistent association with lower impairment across all ADL domains and was indirectly linked to better QoL through improved function.
issues.problem: The abstract singles out education; it does not report that occupational complexity independently predicted better function, so naming "mentally demanding work" in the headline gives it unearned billing.
issues.suggested_fix: Reframe as "A cognitive reserve score — led by education — predicted better everyday functioning."

issues.label: Caveat details not in abstract
issues.as_written: Volunteer online cohort that is heavily female (81%), likely well-educated and Canadian, so results may not generalize. Functional ability was assessed by self-report
issues.abstract_says: Baseline data from 1,571 CU participants (mean age: 64.7±7.6; 81.3% female) from the CAN-PROTECT study were analyzed. ... Functional ability was measured using the Standard Assessment of Global Everyday Activities (SAGEA) scale
issues.problem: The abstract does not state that the cohort was recruited online/by volunteers or that SAGEA was self-reported. Unverifiable from abstract only (the sex split and Canadian setting are supported).
issues.suggested_fix: Attribute these design details to the full paper or drop the "online volunteer" and "self-report" descriptors.

fact_check.headline: What wears dementia caregivers down most isn't memory loss — it's rigidity and apathy
fact_check.notes: Sample sizes (432; 358 with 230 FTLD/128 AD; 172 longitudinal), instruments, and the rigidity/apathy and mood-change findings match; the associations are small in magnitude and the "single specialist center in Sydney" descriptor isn't supported by the abstract.

issues.label: Effect sizes are small
issues.as_written: those were the top drivers of burden
issues.abstract_says: Behavioural rigidity (standardised β = 0.15, 95% CI [0.03, 0.28], p = 0.015) and apathy (standardised β = 0.14, 95% CI [0.02, 0.26], p = 0.020) showed the strongest associations with carer burden overall.
issues.problem: "Strongest associations" in the abstract are modest standardized betas around 0.15; calling them "top drivers" implies a larger causal contribution than the data show.
issues.suggested_fix: Say "those showed the strongest, though modest, statistical links to burden."

issues.label: Single-center description unverifiable
issues.as_written: Single specialist center in Sydney; only 172 participants had follow-up data over roughly one year.
issues.abstract_says: Author affiliations span the Brain and Mind Centre, The University of Sydney, Macquarie University Health, Gosford Hospital, and Royal Prince Alfred Hospital; ethical approval from South Eastern Sydney Local Health District, UNSW and University of Sydney.
issues.problem: The abstract does not state that recruitment came from a single center, and multiple Sydney-area sites are listed. Unverifiable from abstract only.
issues.suggested_fix: Change to "specialist clinic cohort in Sydney, Australia" unless single-site recruitment is confirmed in the full text.

fact_check.headline: Amino acid supplements for muscle loss may backfire in older adults carrying extra weight
fact_check.notes: N=2,994, Hong Kong Chinese cohort, opposite directions for sarcopenia-only versus sarcopenic obesity, isoleucine/phenylalanine 4-year findings, and the dietary/hs-CRP contrasts all match; headline shifts from measured serum markers to supplements.

issues.label: Headline implies supplements were tested
issues.as_written: Amino acid supplements for muscle loss may backfire in older adults carrying extra weight
issues.abstract_says: Serum BCAAs and AAAs were quantified at baseline. ... These distinct profiles, alongside dietary correlates, caution against uniform AA supplementation and suggest phenotype-specific nutritional strategies in older adults.
issues.problem: The study measured circulating amino acid levels, not supplementation; "supplements may backfire" goes further than the authors' caution against uniform supplementation, though the digest's caveat does note no supplement was tested.
issues.suggested_fix: Reword to "Blood amino acid levels point in opposite directions for muscle loss depending on body fat — authors caution against blanket supplementation."
